context_for_next_agent: WORKING TREE IS DIRTY BY DESIGN — do not 'clean up' by discarding. `git status` shows 32 entries: 9 modified + 23 new, the complete booking feature. It is uncommitted only because the orch-add-feature pipeline's GATE 2 requires the user to approve before committing, and the user had not answered when the session ended. The proposed commit split is in the session summary. FEATURE SHAPE: standalone appointment booking (no link to service_requests) with per-slot quota derived from business_hours, auto-confirm, LINE Flex confirmation + Telegram staff alert on booking, a 'คิว'/'นัดหมาย' text command that replies with a Flex list, and an ADMIN-CONFIGURABLE advance reminder (on/off + lead value + unit DAY|HOUR) — the configurability was the user's explicit request over a hardcoded 1-day reminder. KEY FACT: the `bookings` table already existed in production from the initial migration 1349087a4a24 but had no service/endpoint/UI; migration e6f7g8h9i0j1 EXTENDS it (adds contact_name, phone_number, note, reminder_sent_at, cancelled_at, updated_at + indexes ix_bookings_slot and ix_bookings_reminder_due). TWO HAZARDS THE DESIGN CLOSES: (1) oversell — count-then-insert cannot be made safe with SELECT FOR UPDATE because the racing row does not exist yet (phantom); create_booking takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('booking:<date>')) FIRST, then counts, checks capacity and allocates the queue number inside it. The lock is DAY-scoped, not slot-scoped, because the per-day queue-number sequence needs covering too. (2) duplicate reminders across the 2 production uvicorn workers — the guard is claim_reminder(), a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE reminder_sent_at IS NULL checked via rowcount==1; the claim is COMMITTED BEFORE the push, making reminders deliberately at-most-once (a duplicate message to a citizen cannot be taken back; a missed one is recoverable by staff). BUG FOUND AND FIXED DURING SELF-REVIEW, worth remembering: Session.rollback() expires EVERY instance in the session and does so even under expire_on_commit=False (that flag governs commit only). The reminder loop originally held ORM objects across iterations, so the first lost claim expired the rest and the next `booking.id` access — which sat OUTSIDE the try block — would raise MissingGreenlet under async SQLAlchemy and abandon the whole batch. i.e. under real two-worker contention every remaining reminder that pass would silently not send. Fixed by snapshotting ids as plain ints before the loop and re-reading each booking via load_booking_for_reminder() after its claim commits, plus commit-instead-of-rollback on the lost-claim path. Mocks hid this entirely (SimpleNamespace has no expiry behaviour) — 3 regression tests added. VERIFICATION GAP TO CLOSE FIRST: Docker was down all session, so the migration was NEVER executed and `alembic check --target remote` was NEVER run, contrary to the plan's own checklist. Compensating tests (tests/test_booking_migration.py) compare index names between the migration and the model directly, which is the PR #183 failure mode, but that is not a substitute for running it. JUDGEMENT CALLS the user was told about at Gate 2 and may want changed: /admin/bookings uses get_current_staff, which gates on the `access_staff_endpoints` permission key originally meaning live-chat — so restricting AGENT from live-chat would also remove their access to the queue screen; a dedicated permission key would decouple them. Admin cannot set a booking back to CONFIRMED (prevents un-cancelling into a seat someone else now holds). An extra endpoint GET /liff/bookings/options was added beyond the plan because the LIFF page needs to know which services are bookable. ix_bookings_slot is intentionally NOT unique — capacity is >1 per slot and the guard is the advisory lock. TEST BASELINE: the full backend suite is 761 passed + 60 errors, and all 60 errors are 'PostgreSQL not reachable' — that matches the pre-existing baseline exactly and is not regression. The 4 skipped tests in test_booking_create_concurrency.py skip (not error) by design when Postgres is absent.
